scope.flow: EIP-712 signature-based intent verification (depositToIntent, depositToIntentWithPermit) on a chain after a fork/chain ID change

statements.text: The TrailsIntentEntrypoint contract is deployed with its EIP-712 DOMAIN_SEPARATOR computed once in the constructor from block.chainid and stored as an immutable value.
After deployment, the chain forks or the chain ID changes.
Off-chain signatures are generated on the new chain for the signature-based flows such as depositToIntent and depositToIntentWithPermit.
Users call depositToIntent or depositToIntentWithPermit with their off-chain signatures.
The contract validates the signatures against the cached DOMAIN_SEPARATOR that embeds the original chain ID.
Because block.chainid is read only once at deployment and the DOMAIN_SEPARATOR is immutable, the cached separator permanently embeds the original chain ID and is never updated after a fork.
All off-chain signatures become invalid on the new chain, breaking the signature-based flows depositToIntent and depositToIntentWithPermit.
Intent verification is permanently denial-of-service on the forked chain because signatures generated on the new chain never match the original domain separator.
Signature verification should be bound to the current chain ID so EIP-712 signatures remain valid after a chain fork or chain ID change.

The intent verification flows require that signatures used in depositToIntent and depositToIntentWithPermit were generated with the same domain separator/chain ID that the contract uses for verification.

ambiguities: No attacker or authority performing the chain fork/chain-ID change is identified.
The actor calling depositToIntent and any authorization requirements are unspecified.
Permanence of the denial-of-service is asserted; no remediation (upgrade/redeploy) is discussed or ruled out.
Behavior of signatures generated before the fork on the new chain is not detailed.
The precise failure mode of the flows (e.g., revert) is not described.
